title: Macrophages self-generate and refine chemotactic gradients during migration towards complement C5a
experiments_summary: 1. Self-generated chemotaxis assay: Mouse bone marrow-derived macrophages (BMDMs) were placed in an Insall chemotaxis chamber filled with homogeneous 10 nM C5a (both wells and bridge). Time-lapse microscopy was used to monitor directed migration over 18 hours, with a no-C5a negative control and a pre-formed 0–10 nM C5a gradient as a positive control. Higher concentrations (100 nM) were also tested. A hybrid agent-based computational simulation was built using experimentally derived parameters to model self-generated gradient formation. 2. LPS activation experiment: BMDMs were pretreated with 10 ng/ml LPS the day prior to chemotaxis experiments. Both LPS-activated and inactivated macrophages were compared for chemotaxis accuracy and timing in homogeneous C5a. 3. Dose-response to C5a concentration: Chemotaxis chambers were used with initial homogeneous C5a concentrations of 0.3 nM, 3 nM, and 30 nM to quantify the number of cells entering the bridge and forming a front wave. 4. Cell density variation: Cell density was varied while holding C5a concentration constant to evaluate effects on wave timing and cell numbers. 5. Mass spectrometry analysis: C5a was incubated with BMDMs (mouse) and THP-1-derived human macrophage-like cells, and supernatants were analyzed by mass spectrometry to detect C5a-des-Arg (carboxypeptidase M trimming product) and other C5a variants. 6. Fluorescent C5a endocytosis imaging: Commercially available AF647-labeled human C5a was used in Insall chambers with BMDMs. Confocal microscopy (Nikon A1R and Zeiss 880) with 40x/1.3NA or 60x/1.4NA oil objectives was used to image C5a distribution along the bridge and within cells, measuring fluorescence intensity profiles using FIJI/ImageJ. 7. C5a retention assay: BMDMs were seeded in Petri dishes, exposed to 5 nM C5a-AF647 for 1 hour, washed, and monitored by confocal microscopy at multiple time points to assess retention versus secretion of endocytosed C5a. 8. Human versus mouse macrophage comparison: Both mouse BMDMs and human THP-1-derived macrophages were used in Insall chambers with fluorescent C5a in self-generated and imposed gradient conditions. Fluorescence intensity profiles along the bridge were compared. Dose-response curves were generated by counting cells crossing a line 200 µm along the bridge at 18 hours across a range of C5a concentrations. Cell tracking was performed at 3 nM C5a to compare chemotaxis index (cosθ) and speed. 9. C5aR1 receptor inhibition: The non-competitive C5aR1 antagonist PMX-53 (10 µM) was applied to BMDMs chemotaxing in a 0–10 nM imposed C5a gradient to confirm C5aR1's role in chemotaxis and C5a uptake. Cells were pretreated with PMX-53 for 30 minutes, then exposed to 10 nM C5a-AF647 for 1 hour. Confocal imaging on Nikon NSPARC or Zeiss 980 with 60x/1.4NA oil objective was used to quantify intracellular fluorescence, with background subtraction and per-cell intensity averaging. 10. Statistical analysis: All experiments were independently repeated at least three times. Two-tailed Student's t-tests were used for group comparisons. Cell counting was performed using the Cyto3 neural network retrained on macrophage images with Cellpose and Ultrack.
